new_candidates.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
new_candidates.abstract: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/LesionAgent.

new_candidates.title: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving
new_candidates.abstract: Frontier models have demonstrated remarkable general-purpose reasoning capabilities, opening new possibilities for intelligent decision making in the physical world. In autonomous driving, many recent approaches seek to leverage these capabilities through additional adaptation for action output, particularly in scenarios where existing models underperform. We introduce Generalist Action Critic (GAC), a zero-shot framework that combines frontier models' general-purpose reasoning with the planning competence of specialized driving models through an inference-time harness. In GAC, specialized planners generate multiple candidate trajectories and make an initial selection, while a frozen frontier model serves as an action critic that assesses the selected trajectory against scene evidence and either retains it or reselects from the available candidates. The harness combines camera images with spatial overlays, provides driving context and reasoning principles through textual instructions, and regulates the information available at each stage to support trajectory assessment and reselection. On HUGSIM, GAC raises DrivoR's HD-Score to 43.2, achieving state-of-the-art performance among methods trained without additional simulation data. GAC also consistently improves closed-loop driving safety across three planners, with relative HD-Score gains of up to 32.1%. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 further reveal how GAC improves planning performance by correcting up to 52.13% of eligible unsafe trajectory selections while introducing new failures in only 0.67% of originally high-quality selections. These results demonstrate the potential of harnessing frontier models to improve driving safety through inference-time cooperation with specialized planners.

new_candidates.title: Do Alice and Bob Dream of the Oracle? Wishful Cryptanalysis
new_candidates.abstract: For two millennia, offense and defense have forged cryptographic security boundaries. Tools automated calculation and search, while humans drove discovery. Foundation models now mark a shift from automated computation to intelligent scientific discovery. Because cryptanalysis rests on exact mathematical definitions and immediately executable truth, it offers a proving ground for autonomous intelligence to move past security reliant on scarce human attention and explore structures beyond human working memory. Unguided models stall between two opposite traps: authority hallucination, where they surrender whenever prior literature declares a route blocked, and reasoning hallucination, where they produce subtle, unverifiable flaws. Closed platforms and generic agent loops further impede sustained open inquiry. We introduce wishful cryptanalysis, a harness-agnostic methodology that pairs constructive optimism against entrenched assumptions with blinded, zero-import verification against error. Agents first compress reduced-scale theory within provisioned compute so live witnesses certify their mathematics automatically. They then co-adapt primitive, algorithm, and hardware, and climb parameter ladders toward high-round theory. Applied across frontier open-weight and proprietary models with minimal human intervention beyond targets and compute, this paradigm yielded novel attack techniques and thirteen verifiable practical results across Keccak (SHA-3) and AES. These include breaking a fifteen-year-open public challenge and closing longstanding practical gaps, released alongside an early-preview open-source workbench (agent-framework). Extending Kerckhoffs's principle into the AI era, we envision an Open Oracle, an open and auditable public infrastructure that frees cryptographers to legislate security goals, challenge assumptions, distill theory, and co-design resilient standards.

new_candidates.title: A Cognitive Agentic AI Framework for Interactive Process Analysis and Optimization
new_candidates.abstract: Complex multivariable process analysis and optimization require coordinated access to simulation, structured data, machine learning (ML), optimization, and scientific literature, often across disconnected software tools. We present a Cognitive Agentic AI Framework (CAAF) that enables interactive, iterative process investigation through natural-language prompts within an established flowsheet. Following harness-engineering principles, CAAF assigns task interpretation, planning, knowledge synthesis, and context management to a large language model while delegating numerical calculations to specialized tools. Dedicated providers connect databases, scientific-document retrieval, ML-assisted Bayesian optimization (BO), and COCO process simulation. The framework is demonstrated on methyl acetate production. Guided by successive prompts, an engineer explored multivariable relationships, conducted 4,000 BO iterations to maximize carbon conversion yield (C-Yield) and minimize specific energy cost (C-SEC), refined operating bounds, and verified selected candidates through process simulation. Re-simulation of 16 candidates within the restricted domain showed close agreement with ML predictions, with a mean absolute C-Yield error of 0.0085 (0.85 percentage points). The highest BO-derived C-Yield, verified by COCO, was 0.921 versus approximately 0.81 in the initial dataset, an improvement of about 11 percentage points. CAAF also detects and reports non-converged simulations, excludes invalid outputs, and continues subsequent evaluations. The results demonstrate how human-guided agentic coordination can combine engineering tools for iterative analysis and optimization with rigorous simulation-based verification under a fixed process topology.

new_candidates.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
new_candidates.abstract: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.

new_candidates.title: MoHA: Model-Conditioned Harness Adaptation for Long-Video Agents
new_candidates.abstract: Long-video understanding increasingly relies on agentic systems that actively acquire evidence rather than process fixed video representations. Their execution harnesses must coordinate language-level planning with video-level observation and evidence acquisition, yet are typically fixed across model stacks. We therefore introduce MoHA, a framework for model-conditioned harness adaptation that adapts a common initial execution harness to the specific planner and observer models it hosts. MoHA treats the harness itself as a model-conditioned optimization object: under the same task distribution and initialization, different planner-observer stacks can benefit from different executable harnesses. Starting from a common initial harness, MoHA analyzes failed calibration traces to diagnose model-harness mismatches and adapts both planner-side reasoning support, such as overview, memory, and verification, and observer-side capability assignments, including OCR and ASR specialists. After structural adaptation, MoHA separately calibrates observer execution configurations for the hosted model stack. Across three frozen planner stacks, MoHA improves Video-MME Full accuracy by 6.2-27.1 percentage points and Video-Holmes accuracy by 3.1-20.1 points over the fixed initial harness. Cross-model transfer further shows that the adapted harnesses generalize only partially to other models, highlighting the harness as a model-conditioned optimization layer for long-video understanding. Code is available at https://github.com/roverx12345/MoHA.

new_candidates.title: Report2Alpha-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on End-to-End Quantitative Research
new_candidates.abstract: We evaluate whether LLM agents can independently carry out a several-hour quantitative research project: read a brokerage research report, make a plan, and over 7 rounds of iteration propose hypotheses, write factor code and improve it from backtest feedback, seeing only 2022-2023 market data. Like Terminal-Bench-Science, the task evaluates overall research ability; unlike it, there is no directly checkable unique answer: the model must repeatedly propose hypotheses on very noisy data, revise its understanding from experiments, disentangle multiple factors and design ablations without overfitting in-sample, much like complex real-world decisions with many interacting factors. After the research, a fixed rule using only 2022-2023 results selects a low-correlated factor pool from all candidates the model produced, and scores it on unseen 2024-2025 data after removing common style returns such as size and momentum; the same rule on round-0 candidates alone gives a report baseline that "implements the report without iterating". We run gpt-6.1-sol (reasoning effort xhigh), gpt-6.1-terra (xhigh), muse-spark-1.3 (xhigh) and deepseek-v4.1-flash (max) once on each of 7 reports. Of the 28 runs, 19 factor pools pass the usability threshold; the average score is 48.4 (0-100 scale), against 25.4 for the report baseline and 35.9 for the models' own picks. From similar report baselines (17.0-31.0), the models separate after iteration to 74.7 (gpt-6.1-sol), 56.6 (gpt-6.1-terra), 35.8 (deepseek-v4.1-flash) and 26.2 (muse-spark-1.3); their candidates look equally good in training and diverge only in testing, with the leaders proposing more diverse ideas per round and ending with more effective factors in the pool. Evaluating research agents thus requires scoring on frozen future data after removing styles, and measuring "what the research produced" separately from "what was finally picked".

new_candidates.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
new_candidates.abstract: Public benchmarks guide model selection, post-training rewards and claims of progress in artificial intelligence, yet leaderboards report aggregate scores without verifying whether each task's prompt, environment and grader agree on what counts as success. How often that agreement fails in contemporary evaluations, and in which direction confirmed defects move scores, has remained unmeasured across grading designs. Here we synthesize task-level quality reviews of 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations spanning closed-form question answering, document rubrics and agentic execution to assess whether prompts, environments and graders align. Task validity stratifies sharply by grading architecture. Closed-form benchmarks revised after public error reporting reach 92.5% verified validity, compared with 29.3% across six multi-step suites that nevertheless already supply 161 verified complex tasks. Rubric suites fail through mismatches between prompts and reference checklists, whereas execution harnesses add incomplete state assertions, shared-channel leaks and grading-time collisions. Across confirmed defects, 71.7% withhold credit from compliant solutions while 28.3% permit shortcut passes, indicating that raw leaderboard ceilings understate frontier capability on many practical tasks. Grading committed patches inside a fresh container cuts confirmed runtime bypasses from 14.7% in shared containers to 2.7% (a 5.5x drop, and 0% in read-only or static suites), showing how targeted maintenance restores existing benchmarks at low cost. As the initial milestone of the long-term Benchmarks' Last Exam initiative, this synthesis launches sustained expansion across wider benchmark coverage and deeper evaluation-quality dimensions so that pursuing leaderboard gains directly advances genuine model capability.

new_candidates.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
new_candidates.abstract: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-training as predicted from our framework, while joint changes in reward and state entropy provide consistency evidence. States thus provide a quantitative description of how post-training organises agent behaviour.

new_candidates.title: Mjolnir: Finding and Reproducing Vulnerabilities in Root-of-Trust Firmware and RTL with Project-Grounded Agents
new_candidates.abstract: A root of trust (RoT) anchors secure boot and attestation for the system above it, so a bug in RoT firmware or hardware undermines every layer that trusts it. LLM agents now find real vulnerabilities in general-purpose software, but RoT code presents two challenges. First, many security-relevant bugs depend on project-specific trust boundaries and fault-injection countermeasures rather than generic vulnerability patterns, and may cause no crash. Second, without RoT hardware, agents must exercise RoT inputs through the project's own hardware model, mocks, or RTL testbenches. We present Mjolnir, an agentic pipeline that supplies each project's threat model and design conventions to discovery and skeptical review agents, and reproduces surviving findings as proof-of-concept tests in the project's own toolchain. We evaluate Mjolnir on six firmware and RTL targets in Caliptra, OpenTitan, and OpenPRoT. On Caliptra's runtime firmware, it reaches 83.3%-100% precision across three models under blind expert labeling, including 100% on Gemini 3.8 Flash versus 66.7%-78.6% for four single-agent baselines on the same model. On 34 known security-relevant bugs in Caliptra's core firmware fixed after the models' training cutoffs, it finds 10 with Gemini 3.8 Flash versus 7 for the best baseline, and 17 with Gemini 4 Argon versus 12. Across our evaluation scans, maintainers have confirmed 64 of Mjolnir's findings as previously unknown security-relevant bugs: 37 across three models on Caliptra's runtime firmware and 27 across single scans of the other five targets.

new_candidates.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
new_candidates.abstract: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's question and hands the parts to specialized sub-agents, each with read-only access to one source. Domain expertise is written as natural-language procedures that plant engineers can read, review and revise. The system is strictly advisory, with every answer traced back to its sources. We also report organizational lessons from introducing agentic AI into a culture built on safety, traceability and conservative change. Beyond the technical architecture, the Beznau case study examines how an assistant can be introduced into a setting where evidence must be traceable, changes carefully reviewed, and operational decisions retained by plant personnel, paving the way for the responsible use of agentic AI in industrial plant monitoring.

new_candidates.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
new_candidates.abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SGG on Visual Genome and PSG with representative two-stage, one-stage, and multimodal-LLM SGG models. The analysis shows that the components where ground-truth triplets are lost differ across models and datasets. RoHa-SGG improves every metric on all five model-dataset combinations. Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 rise by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for the two-stage and one-stage models. With root-cause guidance, the harness search reaches the final score of an unguided search up to three times faster.

new_candidates.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
new_candidates.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have enabled vision-and-language navigation (VLN) through direct closed-loop perception and action. However, navigation performance depends strongly on the harness governing LLM-environment interactions, while existing harnesses largely rely on manually designed navigation tools, memory, and agent roles. We introduce NavRSI, a harness-centric recursive self-improvement framework that optimizes the navigation behavior of frozen LLMs through closed-loop experience. In each round, NavRSI iteratively collects navigation trajectories and failure diagnostics, employs a designer agent to rewrite the harness, and retains the revisions that prove effective, while the designer accumulates experience from previous revisions so that the harness and this experience co-evolve. Privileged simulator diagnostics guide only the designer and remain inaccessible to the navigating LLM, enabling deployment with a single RGB camera and primitive actions, without task-specific model training or additional navigation tools. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across LLMs from four vendors, with 85.64% success rate on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split with GPT-6-Astra, surpassing the previously reported best by 4.13%. Evaluations on RxR-CE, NavRAG-CE, and a real humanoid robot further demonstrate its generalizability.

new_candidates.title: Sprouting Fields of Conducting Polymer Dendrites as Evolving Organic Electrochemical Frameworks to Interconnect Electrode Arrays
new_candidates.abstract: Balancing high performance with sustainability in microelectronics is challenged by energy-intensive processes, scarce materials and limited recyclability. Inspired by nature, a promising solution relies on the evolution of the foundry model to transient microelectronics, using electrochemistry to grow adaptive circuits on demand and during operation. To this end, this study explores how to harness the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites between stacks of micro-electrode arrays to dynamically interconnect them with voltage pulses. Using propylene carbonate as a solvent, we investigated the dynamics of the electroconvective growth of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), revealing strong structural dependencies between the morphology of the electrogenerated polymer and the confinement of the micro-electrodes. As the system evolves from 2D flat patterns to 3D dendritic structures, the capability of the conducting polymer to locally interconnect specific nodes heavily depends on the size and density of the arrays which directly impact the flow distribution during growth. By unraveling how a device geometry enables the growth of dendritic interconnections on integrated micro-electrode arrays, the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites not only addresses the longstanding issue of heterogeneous integration in microelectronics, but also opens the way to a paradigm where electronic devices learn as they grow in our pockets.
